articles.snippet: Three months since introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corba has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.
articles.text:
In Brief
Posted:
3:32 PM PST · November 16, 2026
Image Credits: TechCrunch (AI-generated)
Julie Bort
Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
Three months after introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corma has raised a $125 million Series A round at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA, the company said. Corma offers AI models and agents trained for cybersecurity defense. It has now raised a total of $185 million from backers, including Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue.
The startup came out of stealth in August. Interest in its product skyrocketed after a series of security incidents sent chief information security officers scrambling on October 21 when a critical flaw was found in PHP , a popular web programming language. Another flaw was found in Node.js , the open source JavaScript runtime environment. Popular open source tool LiteLLM, a proxy for routing requests to multiple LLM providers, also disclosed a security incident. Other incidents were disclosed that day, too. The day showcased the kind of onslaught on security that AI has enabled.
Corma isn’t the only company using AI to play defense. Other examples include Kevin Mandia’s new startup Armadin , as well as Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and other established players, and too many other startups to count. Still, it’s a young market and a necessary one. Corma says it stands out from the crowd by being a frontier AI research lab focused on protection.

Recognition comes amid a period of significant momentum for Positron, following its $875 million Series C and expanding AI inference deployments
RENO, Nev. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Positron AI , the AI inference hardware company built to make generative AI dramatically cheaper and more energy-efficient, today announced it has been named to the inaugural 2026 AI 100 , the definitive ranking of the top 100 private AI companies in the world, published by Newcomer in collaboration with Bessemer Venture Partners .
The inaugural AI 100 recognizes leading private companies driving innovation across the AI ecosystem. Positron's inclusion reflects its progress in bringing purpose-built inference technology to market as growing AI adoption drives demand for more cost- and energy-efficient infrastructure.
"We're honored to be recognized among the companies shaping the future of AI," said Mitesh Agrawal, CEO of Positron AI. "Making AI inference profitable, scalable and accessible takes advanced technology and a business and supply chain built to serve some of the world's largest technology companies. Positron combines deep semiconductor and systems expertise with customer-driven development and investor backing to position us for growth. I'm proud of the business we're building as we serve customers today and develop our next generation of technology, and grateful to our team, customers, partners and investors for their support."
Positron's recognition follows a series of major company milestones. In September, the company announced an $875 million Series C financing at a $5 billion valuation to accelerate development of its next-generation Asimov silicon, ramp production of Titan and expand manufacturing capacity. Positron has also deployed more than 50 racks of Atlas, its first-generation inference system, at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Most recently, the company announced a partnership with General Compute, which is purchasing Atlas systems and has committed to adopting Titan to support next-generation AI workloads.
The inaugural AI 100 evaluated nominated companies and recognized category leaders across four factors: market leadership (35%), estimated valuation (30%), operating metrics (20%), and people & culture (15%). Only independent AI companies that have not had a majority strategic or private equity M&A transaction or a public listing were eligible. Honorees span foundation models, AI infrastructure and compute, developer tools and agents, AI apps, vertical AI, security, physical AI and robotics, and deeptech and AI for science.

Eldridge: Stonebriar Closes $869 Million Equipment Asset-Backed Securitization
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 2:47 PM
Eldridge: Stonebriar Closes $869 Million Equipment Asset-Backed Securitization
Eldridge Capital Management has announced the closing of an $869 million equipment asset-backed securitization by Stonebriar Commercial Finance, an Eldridge-managed company. The financing, designated SCFET 2026-1, represents Stonebriar’s 16th equipment asset-backed securitization and expands the firm’s access to capital for financing essential business equipment across multiple industries.
Eldridge Diversified Credit Fund II also participated in the transaction, bringing together two components of Eldridge’s diversified credit platform.
The securitization is backed by leases and loans secured by essential-use assets across the marine, mining, energy, manufacturing, and technology sectors.
These financing arrangements support businesses that require substantial capital investments in specialized equipment and other income-producing assets.
Asset-backed securitizations allow lenders to package financial assets into securities purchased by institutional investors, creating an additional source of funding for their lending activities.
For Stonebriar, the approach has become an established component of its financing strategy.
The latest transaction builds on approximately $11 billion of asset-backed securities placed through the platform since 2016.
Stonebriar’s securitization program supports its ability to originate large equipment financing transactions while managing funding costs and maintaining access to capital markets.
The participation of Eldridge Diversified Credit Fund II represents an additional opportunity to connect the firm’s private credit investment activities with Stonebriar’s established financing infrastructure.
Eldridge believes the arrangement can provide benefits to its diversified credit strategy by leveraging the funding capabilities Stonebriar has developed over the past decade.
The securities issued through SCFET 2026-1 received ratings from Fitch Ratings and KBRA.
Bank of America served as sole structuring agent and lead bookrunner for the transaction.
BNP Paribas, Truist, and Wells Fargo participated as joint lead bookrunners.
The financing highlights continued institutional demand for securities backed by equipment loans and leases involving essential business assets.
Since 2015, the broader Eldridge platform has originated more than $19 billion in large-ticket equipment finance transactions on behalf of Stonebriar and Eldridge’s diversified credit funds.
The platform finances assets supporting activities such as manufacturing, transportation, electricity generation, chemicals, and other capital-intensive operations.
According to Monitor’s 2026 rankings cited by Eldridge, the firm operates North America’s largest private, independent equipment finance platform by both assets and origination volume.
Eldridge manages a broader portfolio of businesses and investments spanning asset management, infrastructure, insurance, defense and security, minerals, and media.
The latest securitization provides Stonebriar with additional funding capacity while demonstrating how Eldridge can coordinate its equipment finance and private credit activities.

AEVEX Raises 2026 Revenue to $840 Million with Drone Growth
Published on: 14 November، 2026
AEVEX
AEVEX raised its revenue expectations to $840 million in 2026, with growing demand for drones and the expansion of autonomous marine systems.
American uncrewed defense systems company AEVEX has raised its 2026 revenue expectations to $840 million, after recording a 56.5% year-over-year growth in third-quarter revenue, signaling expanding military demand for drones and autonomous systems alongside the company’s expansion into maritime fields.
The company announced revenue of $189.7 million during the third quarter, compared to $121.2 million in the same period of 2025, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $30.8 million, compared to $17.8 million.
AEVEX raised its annual revenue guidance range to $820–$840 million, compared to $700–$720 million previously, and also increased its adjusted EBITDA guidance to $128–$132 million.
Growth Beyond Reliance on Ukraine Programs
One of the most significant shifts in AEVEX’s results is the growth of its core business outside of Ukraine programs, reflecting a broadening customer base and U.S. military orders.
Management stated that core revenue, excluding the Phoenix Ghost and EUCOM Deep Strike programs, reached $137 million in the third quarter, compared to $49 million in the first quarter of the year; new orders for core business also rose to $250.2 million during the third quarter, compared to $65.8 million in the first quarter, reflecting accelerating demand for the company’s systems.
According to management, core revenue surpassed Ukraine-related revenue for the first time since the second quarter of 2025 during the third quarter, marking an important shift toward a more diversified revenue base; the company expects Ukraine revenue of about $36.3 million in the fourth quarter before such revenue declines later, while targeting core revenue between $440 million and $460 million during 2026.
$400 Million Contract… But Actual Value Tied to Orders
AEVEX announced a multi-year U.S. contract with a ceiling value of approximately $400 million to supply uncrewed aircraft systems and related services. The contract represents a flexible framework allowing the customer to issue orders according to operational needs, but it does not mean the entire value has been funded or converted into confirmed revenue.
Management stated that it expects orders related to the contract to be issued during the upcoming period, with potential timing delays due to contractual procedures, but it views the agreement as bolstering revenue opportunities through 2027. The deal derives its importance from reflecting the shift in military demand toward systems that can be manufactured in large quantities and adapted to various mission requirements, rather than relying on fixed-use platforms.
BlackSea Expands AEVEX from Air to Sea
AEVEX’s acquisition of BlackSea Technologies represents one of the most prominent strategic shifts for the company during 2026, adding the marine systems sector to its portfolio and expanding its scope of activity from drones to surface and subsurface systems.
AEVEX expects the Maritime Systems sector to generate revenue of approximately $150 million during 2026, with continued growth the following year. articles.snippet:
Sofinnova Partners, a European life sciences venture capital firm, has completed the final close of Sofinnova Crossover II at €725 million, equivalent to approximately $815 million. The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The post Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:29 AM
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
Sofinnova Partners, a European life sciences venture capital firm, has completed the final close of Sofinnova Crossover II at €725 million, equivalent to approximately $815 million. The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The new vehicle is expected to support approximately 15 companies over its investment period.
While its primary focus will be Europe, the fund will also pursue selected opportunities in the United States and other international markets.
Sofinnova believes the successful fundraising reflects increasing investor confidence in European life sciences businesses developing technologies with global commercial potential.
The fund will provide capital to companies approaching important stages of clinical development and business growth.
Supporting Clinical Development And Commercialization
Life sciences companies frequently require substantial financing to advance experimental therapies and medical technologies through clinical testing, regulatory approval, and commercialization.
Sofinnova Crossover II is designed to support businesses during these later stages of development.
Its investment strategy focuses on companies with promising scientific foundations, clinical validation, and leadership teams capable of expanding internationally.
Sofinnova believes the European market is producing an increasing number of competitive healthcare companies that need access to substantial growth capital.
The firm’s investment approach combines financial backing with industry expertise and strategic support.
Building On Crossover I
Sofinnova’s first crossover fund invested in several companies that subsequently completed significant corporate transactions or public market milestones.
These include LimFlow, acquired by Inari Medical; Calliditas Therapeutics, acquired by Asahi Kasei; and Amolyt Pharma, acquired by AstraZeneca.
The portfolio also included Abivax, which achieved a Nasdaq listing.
These investments demonstrate the firm’s strategy of backing life sciences companies as they advance toward larger commercial markets.
Crossover II has already invested in Hemab Therapeutics, CellCentric, and Neurent Medical.
The fund will continue seeking opportunities among biotechnology and medical technology companies with differentiated products and clinical development programs.
Investment Leadership And Institutional Support
The Crossover II strategy is led by Sofinnova partners Joe Anderson, Kinam Hong, Cedric Moreau, Jacques Theurillat, and David Evans.
The fund is supported by the European Tech Champions Initiative, a fund-of-funds managed by the European Investment Fund.
Sofinnova Partners was founded in 1972 and operates from Paris, London, and Milan.
The firm has invested in more than 500 companies across its history and currently manages more than €4 billion in assets.
Its investment activities span life sciences and sustainability, from early-stage company formation through later-stage development.

articles.title: Sofinnova's Graziano Seghezzi Raises $815 Million to Fix Europe's Biotech Scale-Up Gap
articles.snippet: Sofinnova's Graziano Seghezzi Raises $815 Million to Fix Europe's Biotech Scale-Up Gap BigGo Finance
articles.text:
Sofinnova's Graziano Seghezzi Raises $815 Million to Fix Europe's Biotech Scale-Up Gap
Add preferred source
Sofinnova Partners has raised more than $800 million — roughly three-quarters of a billion — for a fund dedicated entirely to late-stage European biotech and medtech, a direct bet that the continent's problem is no longer invention but the capital to carry companies into commercialization. Managing partner Graziano Seghezzi, speaking at the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London, argues Europe excels at company creation but remains starved of scale-up capital, and that pharma M&A — not European public markets — is the healthy exit route the industry should embrace. The evidence he offers is concrete: a $90 million Series A in Aletheia Therapeutics, a $1.5 billion sale of UK ADC-toxin developer Mirix to Novartis, and Hema now public at a valuation in the low billions. Yet the same conversation carries a counterweight. Seghezzi says Europe "cannot afford" to back fast followers against China, tells portfolio boards to treat China as a speed lever rather than a threat, and confirms Sofinnova still recommends US listings because Europe's public market lacks depth. His 2027 forecast is an up year, powered by record-level pharma M&A and a functioning, if unspectacular, IPO window.
Key Elements
Sofinnova Partners Graziano Seghezzi Aletheia Therapeutics Tea Therapeutics Mirix Surcentrix Hema Novartis Johnson & Johnson Ollin Biosciences Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference Stifel LSEG
Europe's biotech industry has spent two decades waiting for a public market deep enough to carry its best companies. Graziano Seghezzi has stopped waiting and raised three-quarters of a billion dollars to work around the gap instead.
Sofinnova Partners, where Seghezzi is managing partner, has closed a fund above $800 million dedicated entirely to late-stage European biotech and medtech — B rounds, C rounds, crossovers and companies approaching a listing. The fund was announced at Sofinnova's own growth summit in London, a couple of blocks from the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference where Seghezzi sat down to explain it in mid-November 2026.
His thesis is narrow and specific. "We are great at technologies and company creation, but what we're still lacking a little bit is on scale-up capital," he said. The new vehicle is aimed squarely at that missing layer: European companies ambitious enough to want to bring products into commercialization rather than sell early.
A repeat of a fund that already returned exits and listings
This is not a first attempt. Sofinnova's growth team ran an earlier fund that Seghezzi says deployed roughly half a billion euros into European late-stage companies, producing a couple of exits and a couple of public listings. The new pool repeats the playbook at a larger size.
The allocation follows Sofinnova's house pattern of 70–80% biopharma and 20–30% medtech, and stays therapy-area agnostic — the target being, in Seghezzi's words, "everywhere where there is a big medical need and important solutions."

articles.title: Panamint Capital Closes $769 Million Financing for 491 MW Solar Project
articles.snippet: Panamint Capital Closes $769 Million Financing for 491 MW Solar Project Mercom Capital Group
articles.text:
November 09, 2026
Staff
Solar
From: Mercom India
Panamint Capital , a U.S. energy investment firm, has achieved financial close on $769 million in financing for the 491 MW Big Rooter West solar project in Robertson County, Texas. The financing represents the first phase of a $1.8 billion green loan for Big Rooter Power, a 1.2 GW solar photovoltaic project being developed at the company’s Twin Oaks Power Station and Calvert Mine.
The proceeds will fund the ongoing construction of Big Rooter West, the first stage of the project. Construction began in July of this year, and commercial operations are scheduled for August 2028.
The financing comprises a $240 million senior secured construction-to-term loan, a $461 million tax equity bridge loan, and a $68 million letter of credit facility.
Lloyds, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) are serving as coordinating lead arrangers, green loan coordinators, co-syndication agents, and joint bookrunners for the Big Rooter West and Big Rooter East financings. MUFG is also serving as administrative agent.
Panamint Capital expects to close financing for the 658 MW Big Rooter East project in the first quarter of 2027. The financing is expected to comprise a $336 million construction-to-term loan, a $587 million tax equity bridge loan, and a $91 million letter of credit facility, totaling approximately $1.01 billion.
Big Rooter East is scheduled to begin commercial operations in August 2029.
Big Rooter Power is being developed on reclaimed coal mine land at Panamint Capital’s 10,000-acre Twin Oaks Complex between Dallas and Houston. The site has existing operating interconnection infrastructure and includes power generation, surface mining, energy storage, data center capacity, and high-voltage transmission infrastructure.
Panamint Capital said Big Rooter Power will be the largest brownfield renewable energy project in North America.
White & Case and Jackson Walker served as legal counsel to Panamint Capital. Milbank served as legal counsel to the lenders, while CSC Delaware Trust Company acted as collateral agent.
Panamint Capital is headquartered in Incline Village, Nevada. Global Atlantic Financial Group, a wholly owned subsidiary of KKR, holds a minority ownership stake in the company.

articles.text:
Home Business 2 min read Add as a preferred source on Google
Mercor Raises $750 Million in Series D at $20 Billion Valuation
The round includes an employee tender, but Mercor did not disclose how much goes to share sales or new company capital. The company plans to expand AI evaluation and post-training work for businesses.
By John Kim
Published Nov 11, 2026, 4:06 PM EST
Save Share Three miniature task stations under warm studio light / TokenPost.ai
Mercor detailed a broader enterprise AI evaluation and post-training push in a Nov. 10 announcement of a $750 million Series D that values the company at $20 billion.
The round includes an employee tender, but Mercor did not disclose how much of the $750 million is tied to employees selling shares or how much will go to the company as new capital. The company plans to invest in research and infrastructure for evaluations and post-training, along with additional environments where AI agents can practice complex workflows.
Over the past two years, Mercor has developed systems for training and assessing frontier AI models. Its enterprise evaluations use companies’ actual workflows and requirements, giving businesses a way to assess models against tasks shaped around their operations.
More than five million experts work through Mercor’s network and receive payment for training frontier AI models. “Every job in the economy will need its own agents that can perform tasks reliably and efficiently,” Mercor co-founder and CEO Brendan Foody said.
Investors named in the round include Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, funds managed by Apollo affiliates, G Squared, General Catalyst, Glade Brook Capital, NVIDIA, Salesforce, Sapphire Ventures, StepStone Group, XTX Ventures and Zoom.
Mercor’s previous announced financing was a $350 million Series C at a $10 billion valuation on Oct. 27, 2025. In July, the company announced plans to acquire Deeptune, which builds training environments for reinforcement learning. Deeptune’s team had recreated hundreds of enterprise applications over two years.

articles.title: Mercor $750M Series D at $20B: What It Means
articles.snippet: Mercor $750M Series D at $20B: What It Means CASRAI
articles.text:
On 10 November 2026, Mercor announced a $750 million Series D round at a $20 billion valuation. The company runs a marketplace that pays domain experts to train and evaluate frontier AI models, and the round doubles the $10 billion valuation it set in October 2025.
What was announced
Mercor published the news on its own blog on 10 November 2026. The round was priced at $20 billion and included an employee tender alongside new investment. Named participants were Benchmark, Felicis, Fundomo, funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, G Squared, General Catalyst, Glade Brook Capital, NVIDIA, Salesforce, Sapphire Ventures, StepStone Group, XTX Ventures and Zoom. The announcement did not name a lead investor. Crunchbase News listed the round among the week’s biggest funding rounds in its 13 November 2026 roundup.
The previous round was a $350 million Series C at a $10 billion valuation in October 2025, reported by TechCrunch . TechCrunch also reported in July 2026 that Mercor was in talks at a $20 billion valuation .
What Mercor says it does
In the announcement, Mercor says it has more than five million experts in its network “getting paid to train frontier AI models based on their unique knowledge”. It also says it works with enterprises and experts in their fields to build custom evaluations based on the company’s actual workflows. The company says the new funding will go toward infrastructure and research for evaluations and post-training, and toward environments where AI agents can learn complex workflows. It also says it has opened offices in New York and London. The announcement does not break down the network by qualification, so it does not say how many of those experts hold doctorates or work as researchers.
Why it matters for researchers and research offices
The round is a data point on how much capital is flowing toward expert human judgment as an input to AI development. Three practical questions follow for universities and research offices. These are editorial observations, not claims made by Mercor.
Researcher time. Expert annotation and evaluation work for AI companies is paid outside the normal grant and appointment structures. Research offices may need to check how it interacts with institutional outside-activity and conflict-of-commitment policies.
Confidential and unpublished material. Evaluation tasks built from real workflows raise questions about what a researcher may share, including unpublished data, grant content or material under a confidentiality agreement.
Evaluation methods. Expert-written tests are one way AI developers measure model ability. Researchers who read results from such tests can use frameworks such as model evaluation suites and AI evaluation cards to ask what was tested and how.
For background on the techniques this market supports, see RLHF and training data provenance . For an example of a research-level expert-written benchmark, see FrontierMath .
What is not yet known
The Series D announcement did not disclose revenue, expert pay rates or the share of the network made up of researchers. Anyone weighing the opportunity should rely on the terms they are offered directly rather than on funding headlines.
